options.name: AliExpress Open Platform: Dropshipping Developer app
options.unlocks: Full AliExpress catalog (hundreds of millions of listings, not verified number) for search, detail, IL freight and order placement; image search (aliexpress.ds.image.searchV2) = the 'find cheaper' engine.
user_steps: The API is NOT on aliexpress.com. Go to the separate developer portal https://openservice.aliexpress.com and click 'Create Account' (top right). Enter email + verification code, click 'Send email', open the link in the email (check spam), set a password, accept the Developer Agreement, 'Sign up'.

Log in, click your user ID (top right) > 'Profile'. Choose developer type 'Individual' (or 'Corporation' only if you have an osek registration), fill all fields and upload the documents it asks for. AliExpress operations review the profile.

Top menu 'APP Console' > blue 'Create' button > in the list of categories find 'Dropshipping Developer (Individual/Corporation)' > 'Apply'. In 'Reason' paste the English text from docs/suppliers/access-and-pipeline-2026-10.md section 1.2 > 'OK'. Status becomes 'Pending', then 'Active' after admin approval (1-5 days, unverified).

When the category is 'Active': on that category page click 'Create App'. Enter app name, Callback URL (any https URL you control; the store domain W3 or a Cloudflare Workers URL W4; can be a placeholder for now) and optional logo > 'Submit'.
'APP Overview' lists the app with its App Key; open the app to see App Key and App Secret. Then 'API Permission': apply for any inactive Dropshipping permission group.
Set AE_DS_APP_KEY and AE_DS_APP_SECRET in the Claude environment settings (Edit environment > env vars / network secrets). Never paste them in chat.
One-time OAuth with the AliExpress buyer account that will place orders: open the authorize URL the script prints; token handling per doc section 1.2.1.

options.name: Bridge: private WooCommerce hub that importer apps push into
options.unlocks: A password-protected WordPress+WooCommerce site used only as a product database. AutoDS, Importify, DSers, Syncee, Spocket, Doba, Wholesale2B, Inventory Source, AppScenic, HyperSKU and EPROLO all support WooCommerce; our Worker reads products via the WooCommerce REST API v3 (/wp-json/wc/v3/products, consumer key) and can create orders (POST /orders) so the importer app fulfils them. Does not touch decision T1 (the custom store stays the store). Zendrop and Modalyst do not support WooCommerce.
user_steps: Open a small WordPress hosting plan (price not verified, order of $5-15/mo), install WooCommerce, set the site to private/noindex.
Install the importer app(s): AutoDS ($0.99 3-day trial) and/or Importify ($14.95) and/or DSers (free).
WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API > Add key (Read, or Read/Write if we mirror orders). Set WOO_HUB_URL, WOO_HUB_KEY, WOO_HUB_SECRET in the environment settings.
We build scripts/woo_hub.py (search/product/freight CLI as in access-and-pipeline-2026-10.md section 2.3) and tag each product with the source the app recorded.

options.unlocks: Lets AutoDS/Importify/DSers/Zendrop/Modalyst/Spocket/Syncee push products into a Shopify store that our site reads via Storefront/Admin API. Facts (2026-10-10): Starter plan 'isn't available to new stores'; Basic $39/mo monthly or $29/mo yearly; trial 3 days free then $1/mo for 3 months; third-party transaction fee 2% on Basic (Shopify Payments not in Israel); comparison table 'Build headless storefronts: 1' on Basic; Headless channel issues Storefront tokens with no plan requirement stated; dev stores 'can't process real transactions' and 'can't be converted'. Shopify API Terms (updated 2026-10-07) s.2.3.18: may not 'use an alternative to Shopify Checkout' without written authorization; s.6.2.8: may not 'transfer any data you receive from Shopify'. Using Shopify only as a hub with our own checkout risks breaching these; the clean path is Shopify Checkout = T1 option A.
